extracted.intended_audience: BBC editorial staff, journalists, producers, and independent producers making content for BBC services
extracted.subtask_description: Index/overview page of the BBC Editorial Guidelines that lists the BBC's values, standards and topical guidance (accuracy, impartiality, privacy, interactivity, children, conflicts of interest, etc.) and links to detailed guidance and mandatory referral points used by staff and independent producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Editorial Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editorial Guidelines are the BBC's values and standards. They apply to all our content, wherever and however it is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching set of principles that govern BBC content across TV, radio and online; acts as the primary standard for all other listed topic-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Policy Guidance Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Policy Guidance Notes supplement the Editorial Guidelines, with further explanation of their themes and practical tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these notes for additional explanation and practical tips that expand on the core Editorial Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product Placement
rubrics_metrics.description: All programmes made by the BBC, or an independent producer for broadcast on BBC licence fee funded services, must be free of product placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition on product placement in BBC licence-fee funded programming (statement appears as a clear mandatory standard on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and principles related to accuracy in reporting and programme content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes subtopics such as finding contributors and mandatory referrals; accuracy is a core criterion for evaluation of content quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 4: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and guidance on impartiality in BBC output, including how to handle personal view content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what personal view content is and how impartiality principles should be applied in different genres and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 5: Harm and Offence
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on avoiding harm and managing offensive content in BBC output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes material on imitative behaviour and specific topical guidance (eg. alcohol, smoking, solvent abuse, illegal drugs) to reduce risk of harm or offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6: Fairness, Contributors and Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for fairness towards contributors, and consent/handling of contributors' rights and anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses consent processes, anonymity, how contributors should be treated and recorded, and related referral points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 7: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and mandatory referral points concerning individuals' privacy in BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on secret recording, when mandatory referrals are required, and how privacy considerations must be balanced with public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 9: Children and Young People as Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific protections and rules when children and young people participate or are featured in BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains mandatory referral requirements and special principles to safeguard young contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 13: Re-Use and Reversioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and procedures governing re-use and reversioning of BBC material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes principles, full guidance and mandatory referrals for re-using programme material and rights/reversion considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 14 / 16: Editorial Integrity and Independence from External Interests / External Relationships and Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards to protect editorial integrity and independence from external influences, including handling of funding and external relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers advertising/brand considerations, conflicts of interest, and when material or relationships must be declared or referred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 17: Interacting with our Audiences (Audience Interactivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on phone-ins, user-generated content online, mobile content, games, interactive TV, competitions, votes and other audience interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules and detailed guidance for competitions, voting, telephone services, prizes, awards, talent shows, game shows, pre-recorded/repeated programmes, mandatory referrals and a prefatory role for the Interactive Technical Advice and Contracts Unit (ITACU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix 2: Code of Conduct for Competitions and Voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed code of conduct governing the running of competitions and voting associated with BBC output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the specific procedural and fairness requirements producers must follow when conducting competitions or votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access Agreements and Indemnity Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and forms related to access agreements and indemnities for contributors and locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes summary and introductions and practical indemnity/contract forms to manage legal and access risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credits and Logos Online / Online Programme Support Material / User Contributions in News Output
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for online programme support material, correct use of credits and logos, and handling user contributions in news output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance in full is available for online-specific editorial and presentation issues and for integrating user contributions into news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest / Personal and Outside Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on managing personal and outside interests and conflicts of interest for BBC staff and contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out what must be declared, how to manage conflicts, and referral requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Networking, Microblogs and other Third Party Websites: Personal Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on BBC staff personal use of social networking, microblogs and third-party websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on separation between personal and professional use and links to related rules on personal views and conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Process points within the Guidelines where issues must be referred to a higher authority or specialist unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many sections list mandatory referral points (for legal, editorial or safeguarding reasons); the index flags where mandatory referrals apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and Responsibilities / Other Sources of Advice / Training Modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on roles/responsibilities for applying the Editorial Guidelines and pointers to training and other sources of advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training modules are available via BBC Academy on core topics (Accuracy, Impartiality, Strong Language, Violence, Secret Recording, Consent, Children, etc.); the index points staff to where they should seek advice and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Output and Taking Down Online Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and summary on managing live output and procedures for taking down online material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical guidance and processes for handling live broadcasts and removing content from online platforms when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance relevant to financial reporting and journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a topic with summary guidance to ensure appropriate standards in financial coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violence in Drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on portrayal of violence in drama productions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary guidance exists to help drama producers balance creative expression with harm/offence considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability / Editorial Values / BBC Charter and Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles on accountability, editorial values and the BBC's charter-level obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the Guidelines in the context of the BBC Charter and Agreement and high-level accountability obligations.
